overall_summary: The channel's clear growth driver is extreme space phenomena and exoplanet anomalies, with videos focusing on bizarre cosmic environments (e.g., TrES-2b, burning ice planets, supersonic ruby rain) consistently crossing the 1,000-view mark and securing the highest engagement. Conversely, standard psychology hacks and repetitive brain trivia (such as fake memories and song-looping tricks) struggle to capture initial viewer interest, indicating a strong audience preference for grand, highly visual cosmic mysteries over micro-level human biology.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,016 views, 36 likes), 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views, 25 likes) represent the top tier of performance.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space facts focusing on bizarre weather, impossible physics, and terrifying cosmic structures.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) and 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (263 views) show solid baseline performance.
winning_patterns.action: Create comparison-based hooks that challenge the viewer's perception of time and history on Earth.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' generated extremely low views across multiple re-uploads (ranging from 5 to 53 views), and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out standard psychology facts and self-help brain hacks; the market is oversaturated and the current audience is unresponsive.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' peaked at 183 views and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' stalled at 69 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic animal facts unless they can be framed through a cinematic survival or horror-mystery lens.

next_video.concept: WASP-12b, the egg-shaped planet being actively eaten by its parent star.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a high-contrast visual of an egg-shaped planet stretching apart: 'This planet is shaped like a giant egg because its own star is eating it alive.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet is spiraling inward so fast that it will be entirely vaporized in a cosmic blink of an eye.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful exoplanet anomaly trend. The 'egg-shaped' visual combined with the concept of a planet being 'eaten alive' provides a powerful, high-retention hook.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' space catastrophe scenario (e.g., 'What If a Speck of Dark Matter Passed Through Your Body?') to evaluate if the space-loving audience can be successfully transitioned into high-retention sci-fi storytelling.
